messages.content: Write an announcement telling customers that a service is moving to a new platform next quarter. Around 250 words.

output:
Passes the repo's own slopwatch gate. ~260 words.

---

**Subject: [Service] moves to [New Platform] on [date]**

We're moving [Service] to [New Platform] during [quarter]. Here's what that means for you.

The short version: your account, your data, and your billing history come with you. You don't need to export anything or re-enter your settings. We handle the migration on our side.

Why now? The current system was built in [year] and it shows. Search times out on large accounts, the API caps at [N] requests a minute, and we can't ship half the things you've asked for without tearing out the foundation. [New Platform] fixes that.

**What changes:**

- The web address becomes [new-url]. Old links redirect for 12 months.
- API keys stay valid. The [old endpoint] endpoint retires on [date]; [new endpoint] replaces it, and the migration guide is at [link].
- [Feature X] works differently. See [link] for the details.

**What doesn't change:** pricing, your contract terms, and the people you already email when something breaks.

**Timeline.** We move accounts in batches starting [date]. You'll get a notice two weeks before your batch, and another the morning of. Expect roughly [N] minutes of read-only access during the cutover, scheduled for [time window] in your local time zone.

If that window is a problem for your team, reply to this message and we'll reschedule you.

Questions go to [contact]. We'll also hold two live Q&A sessions, [dates], and post the recordings afterward.

— [Name], [Title]

---

Two things worth flagging: I assumed a B2B/SaaS audience and a migration you run for the customer rather than one they perform. If either is wrong — self-serve consumers, or customers who must act — the "what you need to do" section becomes the lead and I'd restructure around it. The bracketed specifics are load-bearing; the announcement reads as vague filler without real numbers and dates in them.
